time_budget.transit_mode: M11 metro from the airport to Gayrettepe, then M2 metro to Vezneciler, a short walk to the Grand Bazaar
time_budget.transit_cost_estimate: Roughly TRY 150-250 each way with an Istanbulkart, plus a one-time card fee. Fares rise often, so check current prices.
time_budget.deadline_math: 18:45 at gate - 60 security - 90 transit back - 30 safety margin = 15:45
assumptions: Early-afternoon arrival at IST means long walks from the gate and moderate-to-busy passport queues, plus 15-20 min at baggage claim because bags are not checked through.

Bags must be stored at the airport left-luggage desk or dropped early for the onward flight. That adds time on arrival, and on return the bag drop happens before the terminal-entry screening, passport control and security.
Rail times assume normal M11 and M2 frequency; the metro avoids road traffic, but the return trip includes building late-afternoon crowds and the long walk from the M11 station to departures.
These core steps alone use about 345 of the 375 minutes before your safety margin, so a trip into the old city is extremely tight.

entry_requirements.summary: German citizens can enter Türkiye visa-free for tourist stays of up to 90 days, with a passport or a valid national ID card. Rules can change, so confirm with the official Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the German Foreign Office before you fly.

verdict_reason: After immigration, baggage, metro both ways and re-check, you have zero minutes in the city. Stay at Istanbul Airport, sort your bag, and enjoy Turkish food and sweets shopping without any risk to your flight.

itinerary.title: Deplane, passport control and baggage claim
itinerary.description: Your bag is not checked through, so clear passport control and collect it at the carousel. Follow the arrivals signs; the walk from the gate can be long.
itinerary.tip: Have your onward booking ready in case the officer asks about your connection.

itinerary.title: Sort your bag: early drop or left-luggage
itinerary.location: Departures check-in hall, then arrivals-level luggage storage
itinerary.description: First ask your onward airline's counter or info desk whether they accept an early bag drop. If not, store it at the airport left-luggage office until check-in opens.
itinerary.tip: International check-in usually opens about 3 hours before departure, around 16:30. Confirm with your airline.

itinerary.title: Late Turkish lunch landside
itinerary.description: Sit down for pide, köfte or a lentil soup with bread, then a glass of Turkish tea. Landside prices are a bit lower than airside.
itinerary.tip: Simit and ayran are the cheapest filling option if you want to save money.

itinerary.title: Rest and recharge
itinerary.description: Find a seat with a socket, charge your phone, and relax before check-in.
itinerary.tip: Set an alarm for 16:25 so you are at the counter as soon as it opens.

itinerary.title: Collect your bag, check in, passport control and security
itinerary.description: Pick up your stored bag, drop it at your airline's counter, then go through exit passport control and security.
itinerary.tip: Queues build in the evening. Do not linger landside after check-in.

itinerary.title: Turkish sweets and market-style shopping airside
itinerary.description: Browse baklava, lokum (Turkish delight), Turkish coffee and spices. It's the closest thing to a bazaar you can get today.
itinerary.tip: Airside prices are high. Taste first, and buy one small box if it fits your shoestring budget.

itinerary.title: Walk to your gate
itinerary.description: Check the screens for your gate and head there with time to spare. Walks to the far piers can take 20+ minutes.
itinerary.tip: Be at the gate by 18:45 no matter what.

running_late_plan: If immigration and baggage claim run past 14:45, skip the landside lunch and eat airside after security.
If your check-in counter is not open by 16:45, ask at the airline info desk right away.
Leave the shops by 18:15 at the latest. Gates at IST can be very far apart.
practical_tips: Cards work almost everywhere at the airport. You only need a little cash in TRY, if any.
Free airport Wi-Fi usually needs a code by SMS or a passport scan at a kiosk. Set it up early.
Your bag is not checked through, so collect it and re-check it. Keep valuables and medicines in your carry-on.
Istanbul Airport is huge. Allow extra walking time everywhere and watch the gate screens.
Bring your German passport or national ID. Either works for entry.
airport_fallback: If you have time to spare airside, look for the airport museum exhibits. Check that they are open on the day.
A pay-in lounge gives you showers and quiet seats, but it costs well over a shoestring budget.
Quiet seating areas near the far piers are good for a nap. Set an alarm.
